_purpose: Git's real error messages, decoded: what you were doing, why it happened, the exact fix.
_tech: JSON, rendered into errors.html by build_pages.py and searched by the finder
_description: Each entry carries the literal error text, a one-line cause, and copy-ready fix commands. Entries that duplicate a full intent link to it via the intent field.

errors.msg: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
errors.why: This folder, and none above it, contains a .git directory. You are outside the project.

fix.n: Nine times out of ten you are in the wrong directory.
Only if this folder truly should become a new repository.

errors.msg: remote: Repository not found.
errors.why: The URL has a typo, the repository is private and you lack access, or you are authenticated as the wrong account.

fix.n: Check the exact owner and name. Case matters on some hosts.
Confirm which account you are signed in as; private repositories 404 instead of revealing they exist.

errors.msg: git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey).
errors.why: The host never received a key it recognizes: no key loaded, key not added to your account, or an HTTPS problem disguised by an SSH URL.

fix.n: If this greets you by name, SSH is fine and the problem is the remote URL.
An https:// URL never uses your SSH key. Switch with git remote set-url origin git@github.com:<user>/<repo>.git
Empty means no key is loaded: run ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519. No key at all: generate one first.

errors.msg: fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/...'
errors.why: The credential your machine sent is wrong, expired, or a password where a token is required.

fix.n: The quickest reset on GitHub: sign in through the browser and git is fixed too.
Then push again; the credential manager prompts fresh. GitHub removed password authentication in August 2021, so a real password can never work.

errors.msg: ! [rejected] main -> main (non-fast-forward)
errors.why: The remote has commits you do not have. Git refuses to overwrite them.

fix.n: Bring their commits in, yours on top.
Never solve this with --force on a shared branch; that erases their work.

errors.msg: ! [rejected] main -> main (fetch first)
errors.why: Same cause as non-fast-forward: someone pushed before you.

errors.msg: error: src refspec main does not match any
errors.why: The branch you are pushing does not exist locally, almost always because there is no commit yet.

fix.n: If it says No commits yet, the branch does not exist until the first commit.
If your branch is actually named master, push that name or rename with git branch -m master main first.

errors.msg: fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories
errors.why: The two sides share no common commit, typically a fresh git init pulled against a remote that already has commits.

fix.n: Typical after git init in a folder while the remote already has a README. Resolve any conflicts and commit.

errors.msg: CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in <file>
errors.why: Both sides changed the same lines; Git needs a human decision.

errors.msg: error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge
errors.why: The operation needs to rewrite files you have edited but not committed. Git refuses to destroy them silently.

fix.n: Set your edits aside, run the merge or switch again, then git stash pop.
Or discard the edits if they were disposable. This loses them.

errors.msg: fatal: The current branch has no upstream branch
errors.why: This local branch has never been connected to a remote branch, so plain git push does not know where to go.

fix.n: Once. From then on plain git push and git pull work.

errors.msg: You are in 'detached HEAD' state.
errors.why: Not an error. You checked out a commit or tag directly, so you stand on a snapshot instead of a branch.

errors.msg: fatal: unable to auto-detect email address
errors.why: Git has no identity to stamp into the commit.

fix.n: Use your GitHub email so commits count on your profile. Drop --global to set it for one repository only.

errors.msg: error: cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes
errors.why: A rebase must start from a clean tree, and yours has edits.

errors.msg: fatal: unable to access '...': Could not resolve host: github.com
errors.why: A network problem, not a Git problem: no internet, VPN or proxy in the way, or DNS down.

fix.n: If this fails, fix the network first.
A stale proxy setting from an old network is a classic cause; check with git config --get http.proxy

errors.msg: fatal: unable to access '...': SSL certificate problem
errors.why: Something intercepts HTTPS, usually a corporate proxy with its own certificate that Git does not trust yet.

fix.n: Point Git at your company's CA bundle; IT provides the file. Never solve this with sslVerify false outside a throwaway test.

errors.msg: error: RPC failed; HTTP 408 curl 22 (or 400, or curl 55)
errors.why: A large push choked, often against a proxy or server limit on request size.

fix.n: Raises the HTTP buffer to 150 MB for this repository.
If it persists, push over SSH instead; SSH has no such limit.

errors.msg: remote: error: GH001: Large files detected.
errors.why: GitHub refuses files over 100 MB in normal Git storage.

errors.msg: fatal: Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists.
errors.why: Another Git process is running, or one crashed and left its lock behind.

fix.n: Close your editor and any Git GUI first: if something IS mid-operation, deleting the lock can corrupt the index. The file is usually a leftover from a crashed process.

errors.msg: fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository
errors.why: The repository folder belongs to a different OS user than the one running Git, common in containers, WSL, and network drives.

fix.n: Common with WSL, containers, network drives, or repos created by another user. The error text prints the exact path to paste.

errors.msg: warning: LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it
errors.why: Windows line endings meeting Unix line endings. Harmless, but configure it once and it goes quiet.

errors.msg: error: pathspec '<name>' did not match any file(s) known to git
errors.why: The file or branch name does not exist as typed: a typo, wrong case, or a branch you have not fetched.

fix.n: See the real file names Git knows.
If it was a branch name, confirm it exists on the remote and fetch first.

errors.msg: fatal: a branch named '<name>' already exists
errors.why: You are creating a branch whose name is taken.

fix.n: If you meant to continue on it.
If the old one is disposable and you want a fresh start here. -D discards its unmerged commits.

errors.msg: error: the branch '<name>' is not fully merged
errors.why: git branch -d protects commits that exist nowhere else. This is the guardrail working.

fix.n: See exactly what would be lost.
Delete anyway, once you are sure. The reflog can still rescue it for about 90 days.

errors.msg: fatal: destination path '<folder>' already exists and is not an empty directory
errors.why: git clone creates the folder, and a folder with that name is already there.

fix.n: Clone into a different folder name.
Or remove the old folder first, if it is disposable.

errors.msg: error: remote origin already exists
errors.why: You are adding a remote named origin to a repository that already has one.

fix.n: Change the existing one instead of adding.

errors.msg: fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository
errors.why: You pushed or pulled against a remote name that is not configured here.

fix.n: Empty output means no remote yet:

errors.msg: Your branch and 'origin/main' have diverged
errors.why: Both you and the remote gained different commits since you last synced.

fix.n: Keep both sides, yours replayed on top. The usual right answer: remote commits land, yours follow cleanly on top.
The remote is the truth, drop local commits. Your local-only commits are discarded.

errors.msg: Your branch is ahead of 'origin/main' by N commits
errors.why: Not an error. You have local commits the remote lacks; push when ready.

fix.n: That is the whole fix. git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline shows what will go up.

errors.msg: fatal: bad object HEAD (or: loose object is corrupt)
errors.why: The object database is damaged, usually a crash, a full disk, or a synced-folder service fighting over .git.

fix.n: Survey the damage.
With a remote, the honest repair: clone fresh, copy over your uncommitted work. Keeping a repository inside OneDrive or Dropbox is the classic cause; exclude .git from syncing.

errors.msg: error: unable to create file <path>: Filename too long
errors.why: Windows' 260-character path limit, hit by deep folder structures.

fix.n: Lifts Git's 260-character Windows limit. Some tools that read the files may still have their own limit.

errors.msg: error: invalid path '<name>'
errors.why: The repository contains a file name Windows forbids: reserved names like aux or con, or characters like colon and question mark, committed from Linux or macOS.

fix.c: git clone --no-checkout <url> && cd <repo> && git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!<bad-path>'
fix.n: Clone without touching disk, exclude the offending path, then git checkout. The lasting fix is renaming the file on a non-Windows machine.

errors.msg: warning: You appear to have cloned an empty repository.
errors.why: Not an error. The remote exists but has no commits yet.

fix.c: git add . && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git push -u origin main
fix.n: You make the first commit; the warning never returns.

errors.msg: fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree
errors.why: You are inside the .git folder itself, or in a bare repository that has no working files by design.

fix.n: If you wandered into .git, step out.
A bare repo (server-side storage) is worked on by cloning it, never directly.

errors.msg: fatal: tag '<name>' already exists
errors.why: Tags are unique names; this one is taken.

fix.n: Move it here, if the old placement was a mistake. If it was pushed, teammates keep the old one until they force-fetch tags.

errors.msg: error: cannot spawn .git/hooks/pre-commit: No such file or directory
errors.why: A hook script is missing, not executable, or has Windows line endings breaking its shebang line.

fix.n: Executable bit first.
Bypass once while you repair the hook. If the script starts with #!/bin/sh, make sure the file is saved with LF endings.

errors.msg: error: gpg failed to sign the data
errors.why: Signing is switched on but the signing setup is incomplete or the key is unavailable.

fix.n: The simplest working setup signs with your SSH key; see the signing answer for the full three lines.
Or switch signing off if you never asked for it; some tools enable it silently.
Reproduces the failure outside Git. A passphrase prompt that never appears is the usual cause.
Add it to your shell profile so the agent knows where to prompt. On Windows, confirming user.signingkey matches a key gpg --list-secret-keys shows fixes most of the rest.

errors.msg: error: Pulling is not possible because you have unmerged files.
errors.why: An earlier merge stopped at conflicts and is still waiting for you to finish it.

errors.msg: hint: You have divergent branches and need to specify how to reconcile them.
errors.why: Newer Git asks you to choose a pull strategy once instead of silently merging.

fix.n: The usual right answer: remote commits land, yours replay on top, history stays straight.
The strict alternative: pull succeeds only when nothing diverged, and asks you to decide otherwise.

errors.msg: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
errors.why: Git wanted to ask for credentials but no terminal was attached, the classic CI and script failure.

fix.n: In CI, inject a token; in GitHub Actions, actions/checkout handles this for you.
On your own machine, store credentials once so Git never needs to ask.

errors.msg: fatal: early EOF (the remote end hung up unexpectedly)
errors.why: A large clone or fetch died mid-transfer: unstable connection, proxy timeout, or a server cutting long downloads.

fix.n: A shallow clone transfers a fraction of the data and almost always survives.
Then deepen to full history in resumable steps once inside.

errors.msg: xcrun: error: invalid active developer path (/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools)
errors.why: A macOS update removed the command line tools, and git on a Mac lives inside them.

fix.n: Reinstalls the tools; git returns with them. This repeats after most major macOS upgrades.

errors.msg: Could not open a connection to your authentication agent.
errors.why: ssh-add needs the ssh-agent process, and none is running in this shell.

fix.n: Starts the agent and loads your key, macOS and Linux.

fix.c: Get-Service ssh-agent | Set-Service -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service ssh-agent
fix.n: Windows PowerShell, once as administrator; the agent then starts with the system.

errors.msg: fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.
errors.why: Your pull is set to fast-forward only, and the branches have diverged, so a decision is needed.

fix.n: The usual answer: remote commits land, yours replay on top.
Or take a merge commit this once. The strict setting did its job: it made the divergence visible instead of merging silently.

errors.msg: You are not currently on a branch.
errors.why: Pull needs a branch to update, and you stand on a detached commit.

errors.msg: error: failed to push some refs to '<url>'
errors.why: The wrapper line under most push rejections; the real reason is the line above it, usually non-fast-forward.

errors.msg: fatal: could not create work tree dir '<name>': Permission denied
errors.why: You are cloning into a folder your user cannot write to.

fix.n: Clone somewhere you own. System folders and other users' paths need rights you should rarely grant to Git.

errors.msg: error: insufficient permission for adding an object to repository database .git/objects
errors.why: Files inside .git belong to another user, typically after running Git with sudo once or sharing a repo folder.

fix.n: Return the repository to your user, then never run Git with sudo again.

errors.msg: error: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/<branch>': unable to resolve reference
errors.why: A stale or corrupted remote-tracking reference, often after an interrupted fetch.

fix.n: Delete the broken reference.
Rebuilds it cleanly from the remote.

errors.msg: error: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/<x>/<y>': 'refs/heads/<x>' exists
errors.why: Branch names are paths: a branch named x blocks any branch named x/y, and the reverse.

fix.n: Rename or delete the conflicting branch; then create the nested name. Agree on a naming scheme (feature/..., fix/...) before the team collides again.

errors.msg: fatal: bad revision 'HEAD'
errors.why: The repository has no commits yet, so HEAD points at nothing.

fix.n: The first commit brings HEAD to life; every log and diff command works after it.

errors.msg: fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.
errors.why: Same family: an empty repository, or a name Git cannot tell apart from a file.

fix.n: Empty repo? Commit first. Otherwise separate revisions from paths with a double dash:
Everything after -- is a path, never a revision.

errors.msg: error: The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by checkout
errors.why: The branch you are switching to tracks files that exist here untracked; Git refuses to destroy them silently.

fix.n: Move them aside if they matter, then switch.
Or preview and delete them if disposable: -fd deletes what -nd lists.

errors.msg: error: unable to unlink old '<file>': Permission denied
errors.why: Something holds the file open: an editor, a running process, or an antivirus scan, most often on Windows.

fix.c: <close the app using the file, then retry>
fix.n: IDEs and dev servers are the usual holders. Persistent cases are the antivirus; exclude the repository folder from real-time scanning.

errors.msg: fatal: '<branch>' is already checked out at '<path>'
errors.why: Worktrees guarantee one checkout per branch, and that branch lives in another folder.

fix.n: See where. Work there, or check out a different branch here.
Or retire that worktree if it is finished.

errors.msg: error: You need to resolve your current index first
errors.why: A merge stopped at conflicts, and Git will not move on until you finish or abandon it.

errors.msg: error: commit <hash> is a merge but no -m option was given.
errors.why: Reverting a merge needs to know which parent line survives.

fix.n: -m 1 keeps the branch the merge landed on, which is almost always what you mean.

errors.msg: fatal: bad config line <n> in file <path>
errors.why: A typo in a config file: an unclosed quote, a stray character, or a section header gone wrong.

fix.n: Opens the file at fault in your editor; the message names the exact line to repair.

errors.msg: There is no tracking information for the current branch.
errors.why: Pull does not know which remote branch feeds this one.

fix.n: Link them once; plain git pull works from then on.

errors.msg: fatal: couldn't find remote ref <branch>
errors.why: No branch by that name exists on the remote: a typo, a deleted branch, or main versus master.

fix.n: The authoritative list of what the remote actually has.

errors.msg: Host key verification failed.
errors.why: SSH does not yet trust this server's fingerprint, or the stored one no longer matches.

fix.n: Run interactively once and answer yes to store the fingerprint. In CI, pre-seed known_hosts instead of disabling checking.

errors.msg: ssh: connect to host github.com port 22: Connection timed out
errors.why: The network blocks port 22, the classic corporate and campus firewall move.

fix.n: GitHub speaks SSH on port 443 too; this tunnels past most firewalls. Or use HTTPS remotes on that network.

errors.msg: error: RPC failed; curl 92 HTTP/2 stream 0 was not closed cleanly
errors.why: A proxy or middlebox mishandling HTTP/2 during a large transfer.

fix.n: Falls back to HTTP/1.1, which the middlebox understands. Retry the push or clone after.

errors.msg: fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly
errors.why: The connection died mid-transfer, usually a large push meeting a server or proxy limit.

fix.n: Raises the HTTP buffer to 150 MB for this repository; SSH remotes avoid the limit entirely.

errors.msg: warning: adding embedded git repository: <folder>
errors.why: You added a folder that is itself a Git repository; it would be recorded as an empty pointer, confusing every clone.

fix.n: Undo the add. Then either delete that folder's inner .git to absorb the files, or make it a real submodule on purpose.

errors.msg: fatal: in unpopulated submodule '<path>'
errors.why: You are standing inside a submodule folder that was never initialized, an empty shell.

fix.n: Fill the shell from the repository root, then return.

errors.msg: fatal: no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules for path '<path>'
errors.why: A submodule folder is recorded in the index but missing from .gitmodules, a half-removed submodule.

fix.n: Finish the removal and commit; or restore the entry in .gitmodules if it should live.

errors.msg: error: could not apply <hash>... <message>
errors.why: A rebase or cherry-pick hit a conflict on this commit and paused for you.

fix.n: Fix the conflicted files, git add them, then:
Or --skip to drop this commit, or --abort to unwind everything. Cherry-pick uses the same three.

errors.msg: CONFLICT (modify/delete): <file> deleted in <ref> and modified in <ref>
errors.why: One side deleted the file, the other edited it; Git cannot choose.

fix.n: Keep the modified version, or:
Honor the deletion. Either way, continue the merge or rebase after.

errors.msg: remote: Support for password authentication was removed on August 13, 2021.
errors.why: GitHub no longer accepts account passwords over HTTPS; a token or SSH key is required.

fix.n: The painless route: browser sign-in wires Git correctly.
Or let the credential manager prompt and store a token on the next push.

errors.msg: remote: Write access to repository not granted.
errors.why: Your account can read this repository but not push to it.

fix.n: The open source path: push to your fork and open a pull request. On team repos, ask for write access instead.

errors.msg: fatal: Not a valid object name: 'main'.
errors.why: Branching from main before any commit exists; a branch cannot point at nothing.

fix.n: Give the repository its first commit; branches work from then on.

errors.msg: remote: Permission to <repo> denied to github-actions[bot].
errors.why: A workflow tried to push, but Actions runs with read-only permissions unless the workflow asks for more.

fix.n: In the workflow file, at the top level or per job. Grant only what the job needs; read-only stays the right default everywhere else.

errors.msg: fatal: your current branch 'main' does not have any commits yet
errors.why: Log, branch, and friends need at least one commit to talk about.

errors.msg: fatal: shallow update not allowed
errors.why: You are pushing from a shallow clone, common in CI checkouts.

fix.n: Complete the history, then push. In GitHub Actions, set fetch-depth: 0 on the checkout step instead.

errors.msg: fatal: Refusing to fetch into current branch refs/heads/<branch> of non-bare repository
errors.why: Fetching directly into the branch you are standing on would pull the floor from under you.

fix.n: For the current branch, pull is the tool.
The into-a-branch form works only for branches you are not on.

errors.msg: error: Server does not allow request for unadvertised object <hash>
errors.why: A submodule is pinned to a commit the server will not hand out directly, or a shallow clone wants what it cannot see.

fix.n: For shallow clones. For submodules, the pin usually points at a commit never pushed: push the submodule's repo first, then update the pin.

errors.msg: fatal: 'origin/<branch>' is not a commit and a branch '<name>' cannot be created from it
errors.why: Your clone has never heard of that remote branch; the start point does not exist locally.

fix.n: Learn what the remote has, then create the branch again.

errors.msg: error: branch '<name>' not found.
errors.why: No local branch by that exact name; a typo, or it lives only on the remote.

fix.n: The full roster. Remote-only branches are deleted with git push origin --delete <name>.

errors.msg: fatal: There is no merge to abort (MERGE_HEAD missing).
errors.why: Nothing is mid-merge; whatever state you are in, it is not that.

fix.n: Names the actual state and its exit: a rebase wants rebase --abort, a cherry-pick its own.

errors.msg: fatal: No rebase in progress?
errors.why: The rebase you are trying to continue or abort already ended, or never started.

fix.n: Confirm the real state; git log --oneline shows whether the rebase finished.

errors.msg: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
errors.why: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is set, as in most CI, and Git wanted to ask for credentials.

fix.n: Inject a token in CI; actions/checkout does this for you inside GitHub Actions.

errors.msg: remote: HTTP Basic: Access denied
errors.why: GitLab's phrasing of bad HTTPS credentials: an expired or wrong token, or a password where a token belongs.

fix.n: Clear the bad entry when prompted and sign in fresh with a personal access token from GitLab's settings.

errors.msg: gpg: signing failed: No secret key
errors.why: Signing is on, but the configured key is not on this machine, typical after a laptop change.

fix.c: git config --global gpg.format ssh && git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
fix.n: Switch to SSH signing with the key you already have; or import the old GPG key, or set commit.gpgsign false.

errors.msg: gpg: signing failed: Inappropriate ioctl for device
errors.why: GPG wants to ask for your passphrase but has no terminal to ask in.

fix.n: Add it to your shell profile; GPG then prompts correctly.

errors.msg: fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
errors.why: The generic tail of every SSH failure; the true cause sits in the lines above it.

fix.n: Reproduce the real error alone: publickey, host key, or timeout, each has its own entry here.

errors.msg: fatal: unable to access '<url>': OpenSSL SSL_read: Connection was reset, errno 10054
errors.why: Something on the network path, a proxy, VPN, or security software, cut the TLS connection, most often on Windows.

fix.n: Uses Windows' own TLS stack, which corporate middleboxes expect. Retry; if it persists, the proxy settings entry is next.

errors.msg: fatal: unable to access '<url>': error setting certificate verify locations
errors.why: Git's CA bundle path is broken, usually after a partial install or an overzealous cleanup.

fix.n: Drop the broken override so Git falls back to its bundled certificates; reinstalling Git also heals it.

errors.msg: error: bad signature 0x00000000 (fatal: index file corrupt)
errors.why: The index file was damaged, a crash, a full disk, or a sync service writing into .git.

fix.n: The index rebuilds from HEAD; your files are untouched. Keep .git out of OneDrive and Dropbox sync.

errors.msg: fatal: LF would be replaced by CRLF in <file>
errors.why: The strict form of the line-ending check: safecrlf is set to refuse converting changes instead of warning.

errors.msg: fatal: It seems that there is already a rebase-merge directory
errors.why: A previous rebase never finished; its state directory still sits in .git.

fix.n: The clean exit. If Git insists nothing is in progress:
Remove the stale state by hand, then start fresh.

errors.msg: fatal: unsafe repository ('<path>' is owned by someone else)
errors.why: The older phrasing of the ownership guard, same cause as dubious ownership.

errors.msg: ! [remote rejected] <branch> -> <branch> (pre-receive hook declined)
errors.why: The server ran a policy check and said no: a protected branch, an oversized file, or a failed lint, and it printed its reason just above this line.

fix.c: <read the remote: lines above the rejection>
fix.n: The server states its rule there. Protected branch? Open a pull request instead of pushing directly.

errors.msg: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/<branch>.
errors.why: GitHub rulesets blocked the push; the lines above name the exact rule, commonly a required pull request or signed commits.

fix.n: Land it through a pull request, which is almost always what the rule wants.

errors.msg: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/<branch>.
errors.why: That branch only accepts changes through reviewed pull requests.

fix.c: git switch -c <change> && git push -u origin <change> && gh pr create --fill
fix.n: The intended road: branch, push, pull request.

errors.msg: remote: error: File <name> is <size> MB; this exceeds GitHub's file size limit of 100.00 MB
errors.why: One specific file crossed the hard limit; the push cannot land while any commit carries it.

fix.n: The large file is in your last commit.
The commit no longer carries the file; push proceeds.
It is buried deeper in history. pip install git-filter-repo first. Rewrites history without the file; every hash after it changes. Then push --force-with-lease and have teammates re-clone.

errors.msg: husky - pre-commit hook exited with code 1 (error)
errors.why: The project's own pre-commit checks failed: lint, tests, or formatting, and the real output sits just above.

fix.n: That is the hook doing its job.
The documented escape hatch for a genuine emergency; use it knowingly, not habitually.

errors.msg: Everything up-to-date
errors.why: Not an error: push found nothing to send. The surprise usually means the work is uncommitted or on another branch.

fix.n: Uncommitted changes do not push. Commit first.
Empty means detached HEAD: your commits are not on any branch. Rescue them: git switch -c <branch>
Empty output means the remote truly has everything, and you are likely looking at the wrong branch or repository on the website.

errors.msg: nothing to commit, working tree clean
errors.why: Commit found no staged changes. Either everything is already committed, or the edits live elsewhere.

fix.n: Untracked files listed? They need git add first. Nothing at all? Check you are in the right folder and branch.

errors.msg: The requested URL returned error: 403
errors.why: The server recognized you and still said no: wrong account's cached credentials, or no write permission here.

fix.n: Confirm which account is talking.
Evict the cached credential so the next push asks fresh; or fork and pull-request if you lack write access.

errors.msg: fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a merge.
errors.why: You named specific paths while a merge is in progress. A merge commit must record the whole resolved state, not a slice of it.

fix.n: Commit everything the merge resolved, with no path arguments.
If you truly must, -i stages the named paths on top of the merge result first.

errors.msg: fatal: You have not concluded your merge (MERGE_HEAD exists).
errors.why: A previous merge stopped with conflicts and was never finished or aborted. Git will not start anything new on top of it.

fix.n: Shows what is still unresolved from that merge.
Backs out completely and returns to the state before it started.

errors.msg: error: Entry '<file>' not uptodate. Cannot merge.
errors.why: That file has uncommitted edits, and the merge needs to change it. Git refuses rather than overwrite them.

fix.n: Shelve just that file, merge, then git stash pop.
Or commit first, so your version merges properly instead of being set aside.

errors.msg: fatal: Exiting because of an unresolved conflict.
errors.why: A command that needed a clean tree found conflict markers still in place from an earlier operation.

fix.n: Lists exactly which files still contain unresolved conflicts.
Edit each one, delete the markers, stage it, then continue the original operation.

errors.msg: warning: refname 'main' is ambiguous.
errors.why: A branch and a tag share the same name, so Git cannot tell which one you mean.

fix.n: Shows which refs are competing for the name.
Spell it out to be unambiguous, then rename or delete one of them so it stops recurring.

errors.msg: git: 'comit' is not a git command. See 'git --help'.
errors.why: A typo, or a subcommand that comes from a tool you have not installed, like lfs or filter-repo.

fix.n: Git offers the command it thinks you meant instead of just refusing.
Lists every command actually available, which settles whether it is a typo or a missing tool.

errors.msg: fatal: protocol 'https' is not supported
errors.why: The URL carries an invisible character, almost always from copying a link out of a web page or chat.

fix.n: Retype the URL by hand rather than pasting it.
If an existing remote is affected, rewrite it the same way.

errors.msg: fatal: Unable to find remote helper for 'https'
errors.why: This Git build has no HTTPS transport, typically a minimal install or one missing its curl support.

fix.n: SSH uses a different transport and usually works immediately.
Or reinstall a complete Git build; on Linux install the git package rather than a stripped core-only one.

errors.msg: Warning: you are leaving 2 commits behind, not connected to any of your branches:
errors.why: You committed while in detached HEAD and are now switching away. Those commits have no branch pointing at them.

fix.n: The message prints the hashes. Naming them makes the work permanent.
If you already switched, the hashes are still here for about ninety days.

errors.msg: fatal: Needed a single revision
errors.why: Git could not resolve the reference you gave, commonly a stash entry, branch, or hash that does not exist.

fix.n: When it came from a stash command, the entry number is probably wrong or already dropped.
Tests any reference on its own and reports precisely what Git cannot resolve.

errors.msg: error: object file .git/objects/ab/cdef... is empty
errors.why: An object was truncated, usually by a crash, a full disk, or a sync service writing inside .git.

fix.n: Reports how much is damaged. Unpushed commits that are still reachable can be branched out first.
If the remote is healthy, a fresh clone is faster and safer than repairing objects by hand.

errors.msg: fatal: transport 'file' not allowed
errors.why: Git blocks submodules and clones from local file paths by default, a hardening change after a security advisory.

fix.n: Allows it for this one command, which is the right scope for a local test or sandbox.
Only if you genuinely rely on local-path submodules; it re-opens the hole everywhere.

errors.msg: remote: fatal: pack exceeds maximum allowed size
errors.why: The push bundles more data than the server accepts in one go, which GitHub caps at 2 GB.

fix.n: Push history in slices, then push the rest, so no single pack is oversized.
If the size comes from large binaries, LFS or a history rewrite is the real fix.

errors.msg: fatal: Out of memory, malloc failed (tried to allocate ... bytes)
errors.why: Packing a large repository exceeded available memory, often on a small CI runner or container.

fix.n: Caps how much Git uses while packing. pack.threads 1 lowers it further.
Avoid the problem entirely where you only need history, not every old file version.

errors.msg: error: unable to create symlink <path>: Function not implemented
errors.why: The repository contains symbolic links and this system will not create them, typically Windows without permission or a filesystem that lacks support.

fix.n: Git checks out plain text files holding the link target instead of failing.

fix.c: Enable Developer Mode in Windows Settings
fix.n: Then reclone: symlinks work without administrator rights from then on.

errors.msg: warning: unable to rmdir '<path>': Directory not empty
errors.why: Git removed everything it tracked in that folder, but something untracked remains, most often a leftover submodule or build output.

fix.n: Shows what is still in there before you delete anything.
Safe once you have confirmed nothing untracked matters. For submodules, deinit first with git submodule deinit -f <path>.

errors.msg: Encountered 1 file(s) that should have been pointers, but weren't:
errors.why: Files matching an LFS rule were committed as ordinary blobs, usually because they went in before LFS was installed or tracked.

fix.c: git add --renormalize . && git commit -m "Convert to LFS pointers"
fix.n: Converts them going forward.
Rewrites history so old copies become pointers too, which is what actually shrinks the repository.

errors.msg: batch response: This repository is over its data quota.
errors.why: LFS storage or bandwidth for the account is exhausted. Bandwidth is consumed by every clone and fetch of LFS content, not only by uploads.

fix.n: Shows storage and bandwidth used; buying a data pack restores service immediately.
Clones pointers only, so contributors who do not need the binaries stop consuming bandwidth.

errors.msg: gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)
errors.why: The resource does not exist, or your token cannot see it. Private repositories return 404 rather than 403 so their existence stays hidden.

fix.n: Confirms which account and scopes are active for that host.
Adds missing scopes. For a SAML-protected organization, authorize the token for it as well.

errors.msg: gh: To use GitHub CLI in a GitHub Actions workflow, set the GH_TOKEN environment variable.
errors.why: gh is installed on the runner but has no credentials; workflows do not inherit a login.

fix.n: On the step or the job. That is the whole fix in most workflows.
Grant the job whatever the command needs; the default token is read-only for many operations.

errors.msg: remote: error: GH007: Your push would publish a private email address.
errors.why: Your commits carry a real address while your account has email privacy enabled, so GitHub blocks the push.

fix.n: Use the noreply address shown in Settings -> Emails.
Rewrites the pending commit with the new identity. For several commits, rebase and reset the author across them.

errors.msg: The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128
errors.why: A Git command inside the workflow failed and Actions reports only the exit code. The cause is nearly always credentials or a missing ref.

fix.n: On actions/checkout, when the failure comes from a command needing history the shallow clone lacks.
Pushing from a workflow needs credentials and contents: write. Read the step's own log above the exit code for the real message.

errors.msg: Error: Input required and not supplied: token
errors.why: An action expected an input that resolved to an empty string, usually a secret that does not exist under that name.

fix.n: Confirm the secret exists and is spelled exactly as the workflow references it.
Secrets are unavailable to workflows triggered by forks, so guard steps that need them.

errors.msg: fatal: update_ref failed for ref 'refs/heads/main': cannot lock ref
errors.why: Another Git process holds the reference, or a stale lock file was left behind by one that crashed.

fix.n: Check nothing else is running: an editor's Git integration, a watcher, or a background fetch.
Delete the stale lock only once you are certain no Git process is alive.

errors.msg: The previous cherry-pick is now empty, possibly due to conflict resolution.
errors.why: Every change in that commit already exists on this branch, so applying it produces nothing.

fix.n: Skip it and continue: the change is already here, which is usually the whole story.
Only if you deliberately want an empty commit recorded for traceability.

errors.msg: No changes - did you forget to use 'git add'?
errors.why: A rebase or cherry-pick paused for you to resolve something, and you ran continue without staging the result.

fix.n: Stage the resolved files, then run the continue command again.
If the commit really has nothing left to apply, skipping it is correct.

errors.msg: hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file...
errors.why: Git opened your configured editor for a commit message and is paused until that program exits. Nothing is stuck.

fix.n: In Vim, or Ctrl+X then Y in nano. In VS Code, close the tab: the --wait flag is what tells Git you are done.
Without --wait the editor returns instantly and Git takes an empty message.

errors.msg: modified: <path> (modified content, untracked content)
errors.why: Not an error. The submodule folder contains uncommitted or untracked work of its own.

fix.n: Shows what changed inside. Commit and push it there, then commit the pointer in the parent.
Hides this noise when submodule scratch work is expected.

errors.msg: warning: unable to access '/root/.gitconfig': Permission denied
errors.why: Git is running as a user whose home directory it cannot read, common inside containers and CI.

fix.n: Point HOME somewhere writable for the command.
In a disposable container image, where ownership checks add nothing.

errors.msg: fatal: empty ident name (for <you@example.com>) not allowed
errors.why: user.name is set to an empty string, so Git cannot build a valid author line.

fix.n: Any non-empty display name resolves it.
Finds which config file set the blank value.

errors.msg: warning: redirecting to https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git/
errors.why: The remote URL still uses http, or omits the .git suffix, so the server redirects every request.

fix.n: Store the final URL and the warning stops.
Check both fetch and push URLs; often only one was updated.

errors.msg: fatal: packed object <hash> (stored in .git/objects/pack/...) is corrupt
errors.why: A pack file was damaged, usually by disk trouble, an interrupted transfer, or a sync client.

fix.n: Confirms the extent of the damage before you touch anything.
Recloning from a healthy remote is faster and safer than repacking around corruption.

errors.msg: warning: The last gc run reported the following. Please correct the root cause and remove .git/gc.log
errors.why: Background maintenance failed, often because too many unreachable objects are held by the reflog or another process was running.

fix.n: Run it in the foreground to see the real error rather than the summary.
Delete the log after fixing the cause, or the warning repeats on every command.

errors.msg: warning: Clock skew detected. Your build may be incomplete.
errors.why: Commit timestamps sit in the future relative to this machine, usually a wrong system clock or files restored from another timezone.

fix.n: Resynchronize the system clock on Windows; timedatectl set-ntp true on Linux.
Confirms whether the offending timestamps are in the history or on your machine.

errors.msg: fatal: Invalid refspec '<value>'
errors.why: The branch or refspec argument is malformed, often an empty variable in a script or a stray colon.

fix.n: Spell the destination out fully so nothing is ambiguous.
In CI, an empty variable is the usual culprit; print it before using it.

errors.msg: fatal: reference is not a tree: <hash>
errors.why: The commit you named does not exist in this clone, commonly after a force push removed it or in a shallow clone that never had it.

fix.n: A shallow clone lacks most history; this brings the rest.
GitHub allows fetching a specific commit directly, which recovers references lost to a force push.

errors.msg: fatal: repository '<url>' does not exist  (during submodule update)
errors.why: The URL in .gitmodules points somewhere that moved, was renamed, or is private to you.

fix.n: Shows every submodule URL as recorded.
After fixing .gitmodules, sync copies the new URL into .git/config where updates actually read it.

errors.msg: error: cannot 'squash' without a previous commit
errors.why: The first line of an interactive rebase list is marked squash or fixup, and there is nothing above it to fold into.

fix.n: Reopen the list and make the top line pick.
Or start one commit earlier so a parent exists to squash into.

errors.msg: error: invalid line 1: pcik <hash>
errors.why: A typo in the interactive rebase instruction list. Git refuses to guess at an unknown command word.

fix.n: Reopens the editor so you can correct the word.
Or back out entirely and start again.

errors.msg: fatal: --unshallow on a complete repository does not make sense
errors.why: This clone already has full history, so there is nothing to deepen. Usually a CI script assumes a shallow checkout that was not shallow.

fix.n: Prints true or false, so the script can decide instead of guessing.
Deepens when shallow and stays quiet when not, which suits unconditional scripts.

errors.msg: CONFLICT (rename/delete): <file> renamed in HEAD but deleted in <branch>
errors.why: One side renamed a file while the other removed it, so Git cannot tell whether the result should exist.

fix.n: Shows both stories before you choose.
To accept the deletion, or git add <file> to keep the renamed version. Either way, staging is what resolves it.

errors.msg: error: Could not verify signature. No principal matched.
errors.why: The commit is signed with an SSH key that is not listed in the allowed-signers file, so Git cannot vouch for who made it.

fix.n: Create the file with lines of the form: email ssh-ed25519 AAAA...
Verifies the fix. GitHub verifies against keys on the account, so a badge there does not mean local verification is configured.

errors.msg: ! [rejected] v1.0.0 -> v1.0.0 (already exists)
errors.why: That tag is already on the remote, and Git will not silently move a published tag.

fix.n: Usually you have a stale local tag; take the remote's version as truth.
Only when you genuinely must move a published tag, and only after telling anyone who may have pulled it.

errors.msg: Cannot rewrite branches: You have unstaged changes.
errors.why: History-rewriting tools refuse to run against a dirty working tree, because the rewrite would fight your edits.

fix.n: Shelve everything, including untracked files, then rewrite.
Confirm the tree is clean before starting; rewrites are hard enough without surprises.

errors.msg: fatal: expected flush after ref listing
errors.why: Something other than Git answered the connection: a proxy, a captive portal, or a server error page.

fix.n: Shows the real response, which is usually an HTML login page.
Clear a stale proxy setting, or set the correct one for your network.

errors.msg: pull request create failed: GraphQL: No commits between main and feature
errors.why: The branch has nothing the base does not already have, so there is nothing to review.

fix.n: Empty output confirms it. Your commits may be unpushed, or on a different branch.
Push the branch first; a pull request compares what the remote has, not your local tree.

errors.msg: gh: could not determine base repository
errors.why: gh works out the repository from the folder's remotes, and this folder has none it recognizes.

fix.n: Pins which repository this folder targets, needed when several remotes exist.
Or name the repository per command, which works from anywhere.

errors.msg: Invalid workflow file: .github/workflows/ci.yml#L12
errors.why: The YAML does not parse or breaks the workflow schema. Indentation and a missing colon cause most of it.

fix.n: Startup failures appear on the Actions tab with the offending line number.
Or lint locally before pushing; a YAML extension in your editor catches most of these as you type.

errors.msg: error: external filter 'git-lfs filter-process' failed  fatal: <file>: smudge filter lfs failed
errors.why: Checkout tried to expand an LFS pointer and the LFS binary was missing, unauthenticated, or out of quota.

fix.n: Installs the filters for your user. Missing LFS after a fresh machine setup is the usual cause.
Fetches the real content once the filter works again.

errors.msg: ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
errors.why: Not a Git problem. A command in the step returned non-zero, and the runner reports the step as failed.

fix.n: Prints only the failing step's output, where the real error sits above this line.
Add to a shell step to echo each command, which pinpoints which one exited.

errors.msg: Error: Container action is only supported on Linux
errors.why: A Docker-based action was used in a job running on a Windows or macOS runner.

fix.n: Move the job, or that one step, to a Linux runner.
If you own the action, a composite or JavaScript action runs on every platform.

errors.msg: Error: Failed to create deployment (status: 404) with build version <sha>
errors.why: The deploy step ran before Pages was switched to the Actions source, so there is nothing to deploy into.

fix.n: Set this once; the workflow then has a target.
The deploy job needs both, plus an environment: github-pages block.

errors.msg: error: chmod on .git/config.lock failed: Operation not permitted
errors.why: The filesystem will not let Git set permissions: typically a network share, an exFAT drive, or a Windows folder reached from WSL.

fix.n: Stops Git from tracking permission bits it cannot control.
Better still, keep the repository on the native filesystem of whichever side edits it.

errors.msg: warning: ignoring broken ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD
errors.why: The pointer recording the remote's default branch is empty or malformed, often after the default branch was renamed.

fix.n: Asks the remote what its default branch is and rewrites the pointer.
Sets it by hand when working offline.

errors.msg: kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
errors.why: The SSH handshake was cut before authentication: usually a firewall, a captive network, or rate limiting on port 22.

fix.n: GitHub serves SSH on 443, which corporate networks rarely block.
Or fall back to HTTPS on networks that only allow web traffic.

errors.msg: WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!  Permissions 0644 for '<path>' are too open.
errors.why: SSH refuses to use a private key that other users on the machine can read.

fix.n: Owner-only access, which is what SSH insists on.
The Windows equivalent when the key was copied from another machine.

errors.msg: Load key "<path>": invalid format
errors.why: The key file is damaged, in a format OpenSSH does not read, or you pointed at the public key by mistake.

fix.n: Prints the public half if the private key is sound. An error here means the file itself is the problem.
Converts a PuTTY or PEM mismatch to the format OpenSSH expects. A key mangled by copy and paste must be regenerated.

errors.msg: sign_and_send_pubkey: signing failed: agent refused operation
errors.why: The agent holds the key but will not sign with it, usually because of a permissions problem on the key or a confused agent session.

fix.n: Clear the agent and load the key again.
Loose permissions cause this as often as they cause the unprotected-key warning.

errors.msg: error: empty filename in tree entry  fatal: unable to read tree <hash>
errors.why: A commit object was written with a malformed entry, usually by a third-party tool or a damaged import.

fix.n: Names the bad object so you know how far back the damage reaches.
If the remote is healthy, recloning beats surgery. Otherwise rewrite past the bad commit with filter-repo.

errors.msg: Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
errors.why: Both sides changed the same lines, so Git stopped and left the file with both versions marked for you to choose.

fix.n: Lists every file waiting under Unmerged paths.
Edit each file to its final form, stage, and commit to complete the merge.

errors.msg: error: key does not contain a section: user
errors.why: A config key was written without its section, most often user instead of user.name.

fix.n: Every key is section.key; the dot is not optional.
Confirms what actually landed in the file.

errors.msg: fatal: --local can only be used inside a git repository
errors.why: A repository-scoped config command ran in a folder that is not a repository, common in scripts and fresh shells.

fix.n: Guard scripts with this before touching local config.
Use the global scope when the setting is not tied to one project.

errors.msg: HTTP 422: Validation Failed (a pull request already exists for <owner>:<branch>)
errors.why: That branch already has an open pull request against the same base. GitHub allows only one.

fix.n: Opens the existing one; new pushes update it automatically.
Finds it when the pull request was opened from a different clone or by someone else.

errors.msg: npm ERR! Error while executing: git ls-remote -h -t ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git  npm ERR! exited with error code: 128
errors.why: A dependency points at a Git URL and npm shells out to Git, which has no key for that host in this environment.

fix.n: Confirms whether Git itself can authenticate; fix that and npm follows.
In CI, rewrite SSH dependency URLs to token-authenticated HTTPS.

errors.msg: ERROR: Cannot find command 'git' - do you have 'git' installed and in your PATH?
errors.why: A requirement uses a git+ URL, and the container or runner has no Git binary.

fix.n: Slim Python images ship without Git; install it before pip runs.
Or depend on the published release instead of a repository, which needs no Git at all.

errors.msg: Make sure you configure your 'user.name' and 'user.email' in git.
errors.why: VS Code refuses to commit without an identity, and its terminal may not see the shell profile where you set one.

fix.n: Set both globally so every editor and terminal agrees.
Shows which file the editor is actually reading.

errors.msg: nothing added to commit but untracked files present (use "git add" to track)
errors.why: The files are new, so Git sees them but is not tracking them yet. Commit records only tracked, staged content.

fix.n: Start tracking everything not ignored, then commit.
The ?? rows are the untracked files. If they should never be committed, ignore them instead.

errors.msg: Error: Unable to resolve action `actions/checkout@v9`, repository or version not found
errors.why: The action reference names a tag, branch, or repository that does not exist. A typo in the version is the usual cause.

fix.n: Check the action's releases page for the current major tag.
Pinning to a commit is immune to retagging and is the safer habit for third-party actions.

errors.msg: The head commit for this pull_request event is not ahead of the base commit.
errors.why: The branch has nothing the base lacks, so the merge-result checkout is empty and the workflow stops.

fix.n: Empty output confirms there is nothing to test.
Usually the branch needs updating, or the work was already merged.

errors.msg: dependabot.yml: The property '#/updates/0' did not contain a required property of 'schedule'
errors.why: Every entry under updates needs package-ecosystem, directory, and schedule. One is missing.

fix.n: Add the missing block; weekly is the sane default for most repositories.
Shows the parse error against the file, which is faster than guessing.

errors.msg: error: could not lock config file .git/config: File exists
errors.why: A stale .git/config.lock is left over from a crashed Git process or an editor holding the file open.

fix.n: Safe once you are sure no Git command is running.
Confirms the config still reads correctly afterwards.

errors.msg: error: cannot run vi: No such file or directory  error: unable to start editor 'vi'
errors.why: core.editor points at a program this machine does not have, common in minimal containers.

fix.n: Or code --wait, or notepad on Windows: anything actually installed.
Passing the message inline skips the editor entirely.

errors.msg: error: Cannot delete branch 'main' checked out at '<path>'
errors.why: Git refuses to delete the branch you are standing on, or one checked out in another worktree.

fix.n: Step off it first, then delete.
If another worktree holds it, that is the one to move or remove.

errors.msg: fatal: <name> - not something we can merge
errors.why: The branch name does not resolve: a typo, or a remote branch you have not fetched.

fix.n: Bring remote branches down before merging them.
Merging a remote branch needs the remote prefix, not the bare name.

errors.msg: warning: Cannot merge binary files: <file> (HEAD vs. <branch>)
errors.why: Binary files cannot be merged line by line, so Git leaves one side in place and asks you to choose.

fix.n: Keep yours, or --theirs for the incoming version.
Staging the chosen version resolves it.

errors.msg: Unable to push: file is locked by another user
errors.why: Git LFS file locking is enabled and someone else holds the lock on that path.

fix.n: Shows who holds it and since when.
Only your own locks, unless you have force rights on the repository.

errors.msg: ! [rejected] v1.0 -> v1.0 (would clobber existing tag)
errors.why: A fetch would move a tag you already have, which Git refuses without permission.

fix.n: Accept the remote's version of the tags.
Or delete the local one first if you would rather look before overwriting.

errors.msg: gh: this API operation needs the "read:org" scope
errors.why: The stored token lacks a scope the command needs.

fix.n: Adds the scope to the existing login without starting over.
Lists the scopes the current token carries.

errors.msg: Warning: Failed to restore: Cache service responded with 503
errors.why: The Actions cache backend was briefly unavailable. The job continues without a cache.

fix.n: Transient by nature; a rerun almost always restores it.
Cache steps should never fail a build, so let them warn rather than stop.

errors.msg: Page build failed: Your site is having problems building
errors.why: The Pages build errored, usually a Jekyll parse failure or an unsupported plugin.

fix.n: If the site is plain files, disabling Jekyll removes the whole class of failure.
With the Actions source, the run log names the failing step precisely.

errors.msg: The custom domain <domain> is already taken
errors.why: Another GitHub repository or account already claims that domain.

fix.n: Remove it from the old repository first; a domain can serve one Pages site at a time.
Confirm the DNS record points where you expect before retrying.

errors.msg: fatal: 'feature branch' is not a valid branch name
errors.why: Branch names cannot contain spaces, and reject .., ~, ^, :, and trailing dots.

fix.n: Hyphens or slashes instead of spaces.
Validates a name before you use it in a script.

errors.msg: warning: more than one credential helper configured
errors.why: Several helpers are set across config levels, and they can answer with different accounts.

fix.n: Lists every helper and the file that set it.
Clear them, then set exactly one.

errors.msg: remote: Permission to <owner>/<repo>.git denied to <other-username>.
errors.why: Git authenticated as a different account than the one with access: usually a cached credential.

fix.n: Shows which account is active for this host.
Clear the stored credential and sign in as the right account.

errors.msg: Hi <other-user>! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.
errors.why: Not an error, but the name is the wrong account: SSH offered a different key than you intended.

fix.n: The verbose output names which key file was accepted.
Pin the key per repository so the right identity is used.

errors.msg: Nothing to do  (interactive rebase exited immediately)
errors.why: The instruction list was saved empty or every line was commented out, so the rebase had nothing to run.

fix.n: Start again and leave the pick lines in place.
An emptied list can drop commits; the reflog has the pre-rebase tip if so.

errors.msg: error: a cherry-pick or revert is already in progress  hint: try "git cherry-pick (--continue | --abort | --quit)"
errors.why: An earlier pick stopped on a conflict and was never finished.

fix.n: Shows what is unresolved from the previous attempt.
Or --continue once staged, or --quit to leave the changes and forget the operation.

errors.msg: fatal: unable to access '<url>': gnutls_handshake() failed: Error in the pull function.
errors.why: The TLS handshake failed, typically an intercepting proxy or an outdated Git build.

fix.n: Forces the simpler protocol, which many corporate proxies handle correctly.
SSH sidesteps TLS inspection entirely.

errors.msg: fatal: unable to access '<url>': Empty reply from server
errors.why: Something closed the connection without answering: a proxy, a firewall, or a captive portal.

fix.n: Shows any proxy Git is configured to use.
The verbose output names whatever actually answered.

errors.msg: fatal: protocol error: bad line length character: <chars>
errors.why: The server sent something Git could not parse, usually an HTML error page or an SSH login banner.

fix.n: A banner or message of the day printed here will break the protocol.
Shows the raw exchange so you can see what arrived instead of Git data.

errors.msg: fatal: cannot fork() for index-pack: Resource temporarily unavailable
errors.why: The machine hit a process or memory limit while unpacking the transfer.

fix.n: Fewer threads means less memory for the unpack.
A smaller transfer avoids the heavy unpack altogether.

errors.msg: error: refs/heads/<name> does not point to a valid object!
errors.why: The ref file names an object this repository no longer holds.

fix.n: Confirms what is missing before you change anything.
Delete the broken ref, then recreate the branch from a good commit or the remote.

errors.msg: error: unable to read sha1 file of <path> (<hash>)
errors.why: An object the index references is missing from the object store.

fix.n: Lists every missing object.
If the remote is healthy, recloning beats object surgery.

errors.msg: warning: multiple merge bases found, using the first
errors.why: History has more than one common ancestor, usually after criss-cross merges.

fix.n: Lists them all so you can see the shape.
The merge still proceeds; this is information, not a failure.

errors.msg: fatal: <path>: '<path>' is outside repository at '<root>'
errors.why: The path argument resolves above the repository root.

fix.n: Prints the root, so you can see where you actually are.
Run the command from inside the repository.

errors.msg: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
errors.why: You asked Git to add a file that an ignore rule excludes.

fix.n: Names the file, line, and pattern responsible.
Force it in when the rule is too broad, or narrow the rule instead.

errors.msg: error: Sparse checkout leaves no entry on working directory
errors.why: The sparse patterns match nothing, so the checkout would be empty.

fix.n: Shows the patterns currently in force.
Use a path that exists, or disable sparse checkout to see everything again.

errors.msg: Aborting commit due to empty commit message.
errors.why: The editor closed with no text, so Git refused to record the commit.

fix.n: Pass the message inline and skip the editor.
Without --wait the editor returns instantly and the message stays empty.

errors.msg: no changes added to commit (use "git add" and/or "git commit -a")
errors.why: Files are modified but nothing is staged, so there is nothing to record.

fix.n: Stage what belongs in this commit.
Or commit every tracked modification at once, which still skips untracked files.

errors.msg: Your name and email address were configured automatically based on your username and hostname.
errors.why: Git guessed an identity from the machine, and commits made this way are attributed to nobody.

fix.n: Set it before committing anything you care about.
Fixes the last commit once the identity is right.

errors.msg: fatal: invalid date format: <value>
errors.why: The date string does not match any format Git understands.

fix.n: ISO 8601 always parses.
Set the committer date too when both should agree.

errors.msg: error: dst refspec <name> matches more than one
errors.why: A tag and a branch share that name, so the push target is ambiguous.

fix.n: Spell out which one you mean.
Better, rename one: sharing a name between a tag and a branch invites this forever.

errors.msg: error: unable to delete '<branch>': remote ref does not exist
errors.why: The branch is already gone from the remote, or the name is misspelled.

fix.n: Lists exactly what the server has right now.
Your local view was stale; pruning refreshes it.

errors.msg: fatal: No configured push destination.
errors.why: This branch has no remote to push to, and none was given on the command line.

fix.n: Add the remote if the repository has none.
Set the upstream so later pushes need no arguments.

errors.msg: You have exceeded a secondary rate limit. Please wait a few minutes before you try again.
errors.why: Too many writes in a short window. This limit is separate from the hourly quota.

fix.n: The primary quota often still looks healthy, which is why this surprises scripts.
Back off and retry; secondary limits clear in minutes, not hours.

errors.msg: Error: Resource not accessible by integration
errors.why: The workflow token lacks permission for what the step attempted.

fix.n: Grant the one scope the step needs, at job level.
Check the repository default has not been pinned to read-only.

errors.msg: At least 1 approving review is required by reviewers with write access.
errors.why: A ruleset requires approvals this pull request does not have.

fix.n: Shows what is still outstanding.
Solo maintainers usually want this at zero while keeping status checks required.

errors.msg: Required status check "build" is expected.
errors.why: A required check never reported, so the pull request waits indefinitely.

fix.n: Shows which check is missing rather than failing.
Remove renamed or skipped checks from the required list.

errors.msg: This branch has conflicts that must be resolved
errors.why: The pull request cannot merge until the overlap with its base branch is settled.

fix.c: gh pr checkout <number> && git merge main
fix.n: Resolve locally, where you can test the result.
For small text conflicts the in-browser editor is enough.

errors.msg: This repository has been archived by the owner. It is now read-only.
errors.why: Archived repositories reject pushes, issues, and pull requests by design.

fix.n: Only the owner can reopen it.
To carry the work on elsewhere, fork it.

errors.msg: Your SSO session has expired or you must re-authenticate to access this organization.
errors.why: A SAML-protected organization needs the credential or session authorized again.

fix.c: Settings -> Developer settings -> Tokens -> Configure SSO
fix.n: Authorize the token for that organization.
Signing in again refreshes the SSO session.

errors.msg: No space left on device
errors.why: The runner filled its disk, usually with container layers or build output.

fix.n: Add it as a step before the failure point to confirm.
Free space mid-job, or move heavy work to a larger runner.

errors.msg: Error: Unable to find any artifacts for the associated workflow run
errors.why: The download ran for an artifact that was never uploaded, or belongs to a different run.

fix.n: Confirm the uploading job actually completed.
Downstream jobs must declare the dependency, or they race the upload.

errors.msg: The job was canceled because "ubuntu-latest" failed
errors.why: One matrix combination failed and fail-fast cancelled the others.

fix.n: Let every combination finish so you see the whole picture.
Read the combination that genuinely failed first.

errors.msg: This scheduled workflow is disabled because the repository has been inactive for 60 days
errors.why: Scheduled runs pause automatically after a long quiet period.

fix.n: Re-enable it in one command.
Any activity resets the inactivity clock.

errors.msg: error parsing called workflow: workflow was not found
errors.why: The reusable workflow path or ref does not resolve for the caller.

fix.n: The path must be complete, including .github/workflows.
Confirms the file exists on that ref and is visible to the caller.

errors.msg: npm ERR! code EINTEGRITY  npm ERR! integrity checksum failed when using sha512
errors.why: The lockfile records a hash that no longer matches what the registry served.

fix.n: Regenerate the lockfile, then commit it.
Review the regenerated file: an unexpected change of source is worth understanding.

errors.msg: ERROR: Command errored out with exit status 128: git clone -q <url>
errors.why: pip shelled out to Git and Git failed, almost always on authentication.

fix.n: Reproduces the failure with pip out of the way.
In CI, supply credentials in the URL or through a Git config rewrite.

errors.msg: verifying <module>: checksum mismatch  SECURITY ERROR
errors.why: The module checksum differs from the recorded sum, which can mean a moved tag or a poisoned cache.

fix.n: Clears a bad cache entry.
For private modules, exclude them from the public sum database rather than disabling verification.

errors.msg: failed to solve: failed to read dockerfile: error fetching default branch
errors.why: Docker tried to build from a Git URL it could not read.

fix.n: Confirm the reference resolves and that you have access.
Build from a local checkout when the repository is private.

errors.msg: Failed to execute git clone --mirror -- '<url>'
errors.why: Composer's Git call failed, usually credentials for a private package.

fix.n: Tests the same access Composer needs.
Give Composer a token rather than relying on interactive prompts.

errors.msg: Git not found. Install Git, or configure git.path in your settings.
errors.why: VS Code cannot locate a Git binary on PATH.

fix.n: If this fails in a terminal too, Git is genuinely missing.
Point the setting at the binary when PATH cannot be fixed.

errors.msg: Push rejected: Push to origin/main was rejected
errors.why: The IDE is reporting a non-fast-forward push behind a friendlier dialog.

fix.n: Shows exactly what you are missing.
Bring your work on top of theirs, then push.

errors.msg: Agreeing to the Xcode/iOS license requires admin privileges
errors.why: macOS ships Git through the developer tools, which refuse to run until the licence is accepted.

fix.n: Accept it once.
Or install a Git that does not depend on Xcode at all.

errors.msg: error: unable to create file <name>: Invalid argument
errors.why: Windows reserves names such as aux, con, and nul, so a checkout containing one fails.

fix.n: Keeps Git from creating paths Windows cannot handle safely.
Or exclude the offending path when you need only part of the tree.

errors.msg: warning: the following paths have collided (e.g. 'README.md' and 'readme.md')
errors.why: Two paths differ only by case, which a case-insensitive filesystem cannot represent at once.

fix.n: Lists the colliding pairs.
Rename one from a case-sensitive machine, or check out only one of them.
